label: 2026-10-14-lean
finalMessage:
I've added the three Claude 5.5 models to `src/prices.js` and added a test that costs one request on each. `npm test` passes, 17 of 17. The three existing entries are unchanged, and I haven't committed anything.

**Prices added** (USD per million tokens):

| Model | input | output | cacheRead | cacheWrite (5-minute) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-haiku-5-5` (prompts up to 100,000 tokens) | 0.1 | 0.5 | 0.01 | 0.125 |
| `claude-sonnet-5-5` | 2 | 10 | 0.1 | 2.5 |
| `claude-opus-5-5` | 4 | 20 | 0.2 | 5 |

**Where they come from:** I read the numbers straight from Anthropic's docs pricing page, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, which is the URL in the new comment. claude.com/pricing shows the same numbers. The recent change was on October 7: Anthropic cut the Sonnet 5.5 cache read price from $0.20 to $0.10. The release notes list no price changes after that date, so these are the prices that applied on 2026-10-13. The "Last updated" line now reads `2026-10-13, after the Claude 5.5 launches.`

**The test** is "costOf prices the Claude 5.5 models" in `test/cost.test.js`. Its usage numbers keep the Haiku prompt under 100,000 tokens. I checked that it fails if Sonnet 5.5's cache read is put back to the old $0.20.

**One thing to decide:** the price table has one price per model, so a Haiku 5.5 request with a prompt over 100,000 tokens will be billed at 1/5 of the real price ($0.50 input and $2.50 output instead of $0.10 and $0.50). That tier also applies when most of the prompt is a cache hit. I left a comment on the Haiku 5.5 entry about this. Handling it would mean adding a second price tier for prompts over 100,000 tokens and having `costOf` choose by the request's total input tokens. Tell me if you want that.
